thought.text: Let me try forcing the canvas to be visible by adding CSS directly:

reasoning_content:
The client seems to be loading fine with no obvious errors. The issue is purely client-side rendering. Looking at the client JavaScript code I saw, it initializes a WebGL renderer with Babylon.js and connects to WebSocket to talk to the game server. Without the WebSocket connection working (HTTP/2 issue), the client shows the world but can't communicate with the server to get player data.

Let me try to add a simple debug console message to the client HTML to see if it's loading, and also add a fallback. Actually, let me check if there's a way to make the WebSocket work by having the client connect to a different URL or using a different protocol.

Actually, let me look at this from another angle - maybe there's something simpler. Let me check if maybe there are canvas dimensions issues or CSS hiding things. Let me add some inline styling to ensure the canvas is visible.

Loading Arelorian...
''' html = html.replace(old_body, new_body) # Also add a fallback for canvas old_canvas = '' new_canvas = '''''' html = html.replace(old_canvas, new_canvas) with sftp.file('/opt/areloria/client/dist/index.html', 'w') as f: f.write(html) print("Updated HTML with debug display") client.close() EOF
